The fortitudes of belief
Forthwith sell the gambler
The commonplace stakes
Thus, as fortune first favours the made,
Bravery is slated by knowing relief
Immature, slayed by the retiring wiles of mind
That settle down in defeat before
The honest, gallant settling of scores.
Never more and nevertheless,
Belief is the castle wall ever without rest,
Guarded day and night by faithful ignorance,
keeper of a law unparsed, without test.
Simply operant is this minding,
This vigil at the rampart,
Til gleaming daylight comes finding
Part by part the castle halls impressed -
The castle walls are as nothing to Truth,
The everyday beaming of jest!
